# Purdue University Industrial-Organizational Psychology

> The Ph.D. program in industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology at Purdue University, West Lafayette. Among the oldest I-O programs in the world, conferring its first degree in 1939. It has graduated more PhDs and produced more SIOP Fellows than any other I-O program and is among the top-ranked programs in the nation. Training follows a science-practice model: students are trained both as researchers and as applied scientists equipped to work with organizations on human resource issues.

## Key facts

- Part of Purdue University's Department of Psychological Sciences, West Lafayette, Indiana. Not affiliated with the Purdue Global I-O Psychology program.
- Offers a Ph.D. only; there is no terminal master's degree.
- First degree conferred in 1939.
- Intensive, apprenticeship-based training: each student works closely with their advisor and can collaborate with multiple faculty. Only a few students are admitted each year.
- All admitted students are funded, with a five-year funding guarantee, a nine-month stipend, and a tuition waiver, contingent on good progress toward the PhD.
- Current students' average undergraduate GPA is 3.64.
- Core faculty: Alex Harris-Watson, Franki Y. H. Kung, Brooke N. Macnamara, Louis Tay, Sang Eun Woo.
- PAGSIP, the Purdue Association of Graduate Students in Industrial Psychology, was established in 1949. Its newsletter archive runs from 1952 to the present.
- The program hosts the Ernest J. McCormick Memorial Lecture.
- The application deadline is December 1, for fall entry only. The GRE General Test is required; the Psychology subject test is not.
- Most students complete the Ph.D. in four to six years. Milestones are a master's thesis, a two-part preliminary examination, and a dissertation.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/): Program overview, rankings, and where to start.
- [Our Program](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/our-program): The science-practice model, Purdue and West Lafayette, and program awards.
- [Curriculum and Degree Requirements](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/curriculum): Statistics sequence, the four I-O core courses, seminars and colloquium, and the master's thesis, preliminary examination and dissertation milestones.
- [People](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/people): Faculty, courtesy faculty at the Mitch Daniels School of Business, and current graduate students with research interests.
- [Admissions](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/admissions): Admissions criteria, funding, how to apply, and application guidance.
- [Admissions FAQ](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/admissions/faq): Deadline, how to apply, required materials, the GRE, fees and waivers, funding, English proficiency requirements, and GPA.
- [News](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/news): Program news.
- [Ernest J. McCormick Memorial Lecture](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/news/mccormick-lecture): Past speakers, talk titles and abstracts for the program's memorial lecture series.
- [What Is I-O Psychology?](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/i-o-psychology-resources): What the field is, what I-O psychologists do, how it differs from organizational behavior and HR, and job prospects.
- [Contact](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/contact): Who to contact about applications, faculty research, PAGSIP and alumni updates, plus the department's address.
- [PAGSIP](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/purdue-association-of-graduate-students-in-industrial-psychology-pagsip): History, current members, honorary committee, and archive.
- [Alumni](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/purdue-association-of-graduate-students-in-industrial-psychology-pagsip/alumni): Recent graduates, their positions, and alumni interviews.
- [Newsletters](https://www.purdueiopsych.com/purdue-association-of-graduate-students-in-industrial-psychology-pagsip/newsletters): The PAGSIP newsletter archive, 1952 to today.
